thread.title: Stocks Rise In Falling Volume; 3 Retailers Near Highs

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stocks Rise In Falling Volume; 3 Retailers Near Highs
text:
U.S. stock indexes sprinted ahead midday Wednesday, but volume continued its recent pattern of declining volume.
X The Nasdaq and the small cap Russell 2000 advanced 1% and 1.3% respectively, while the S&P 500 added 0.7%. The blue chip Dow Jones industrial average rose 0.6%.
Volume in the stock market today was lower vs. the previous session on both major exchanges. Trade is on track to decline for a fourth consecutive session.
The FANG stocks were showing strength, as each rose in above-average volume. Facebook ( FB ) popped 1.5% but is still trying to retake its 50-day line. Amazon.com ( AMZN ) rose 1.8%, padding its cushion above the 50-day line. Netflix ( NFLX ) gained 2% as it headed toward its sixth gain in the past seven sessions. Alphabet ( GOOGL ) climbed 1.8% as it tried to add space above its 50-day line. Apple ( AAPL ) glided 1% higher as it held above its 50-day line.
None of the FANG stocks are positioned for a buy, but investors who already hold a position aren't seeing any sell signals now.

Retail-Apparel/Shoes advanced 1.8%. Within the group, Urban Outfitters ( URBN ) added 2%, now trading just 1% off a new high. Lululemon Athlectica ( LULU ) tacked on 1.5% to 1% off its high. American Eagle Outfitters ( AEO ) surged 3.5% to about 2% off its high.
Urban Outfitters' fiscal year ends in January. The company will release fiscal 2018 results March 6 after the close.
Analysts expect earnings to drop 16% vs. fiscal 2017. The Street expects the high-end fashion apparel and home goods company to grow earnings 24% in fiscal 2019.
Lululemon's fiscal year also ends in January. Analysts see earnings rising 18% in fiscal 2018 and then 19% in fiscal 2019. Lululemon is a member of IBD Leaderboard .
American Eagle Outfitters, which also ends its fiscal year in January, is expected to see an earnings decline of 7% in fiscal 2018.
In fiscal 2019, earnings are expected to rise 17%.
Financial Data In economic news, mortgage applications dropped 6.6% for the week.
Weekly retail same-store sales for chains, discounters and department stores rolled in at 3.7% vs. the previous week's 2.8% gain.
The flash composite Purchasing Managers Index for February came in at 55.9, above the entire range of estimates.
Existing-home sales for January missed estimates. The number was an annualized rate of 5.38 million, which was below the lowest estimate in the range.
At 2 p.m. ET, the Federal Reserve will release the minutes from the Jan. 30-31 meeting.
